name: Asset Plus Limited
overview: Asset Plus Limited (formerly NPT Limited) is an NZX-listed commercial property investment company externally managed by Centuria Funds Management (NZ) Limited, structured as a Portfolio Investment Entity (PIE) for tax-efficient distributions. Following the November 2024 sale of 35 Graham Street, the company now owns a single asset, the 6-8 Munroe Lane office building in Albany, Auckland, independently valued at $105.5 million as at 31 March 2026 and ~75.6% occupied. Management's stated strategy, reaffirmed at the 6 August 2026 Annual Meeting, is to complete the lease-up of Munroe Lane, then sell the property and put an orderly wind-up of the Company to a shareholder vote - this is a terminating single-asset liquidation vehicle, not a going-concern compounder, and should be valued as such.

business_model.summary: Asset Plus earns net rental income from a single Auckland office building (Munroe Lane) under an externally managed, PIE-taxed structure. Revenue is currently constrained by elevated vacancy (partial lease-up in progress); the company pays management, director, audit and other administration fees to run a very small asset base, and has no debt (0% LVR) since repaying all borrowings on the November 2024 Graham Street sale. The business is explicitly being run toward a sale-and-wind-up outcome rather than for ongoing growth - management and the Board have no acquisition mandate.

revenue_streams.name: Munroe Lane net rental income
revenue_streams.trend: growing (from a low base as vacancy fills; WALE 9.4 years at Mar-2026)

business_model.customer_type: B2B commercial office/retail tenants (e.g., Aderant - legal/business software, lease commenced 1-Feb-2026; MILK Orthodontics - 12-year ground-floor lease pending commencement; other Albany-market office/retail tenants)
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% Auckland, New Zealand (Albany, North Shore office market) - single property, single market

main_competitors: Direct landlords and sublease space in the Albany/North Shore office market
competitive_position.market_position: Sub-scale, single-asset participant in the NZ listed property sector; not a going-concern competitor for new capital or acquisitions given its wind-down posture - it does not compete for growth capital or new deals, only for tenants at one building

moat_factors.description: This is not a business with a durable competitive advantage to protect; it is a single asset being prepared for sale. Any 'competitive advantage' language should be read as tenant-attraction factors for one building, not a compounding moat

Munroe Lane is a 5 Star Green Star-rated, relatively modern building targeting a 5-star NABERSNZ energy rating, which helps it compete for corporate tenants seeking sustainable premises and should support a better exit multiple than older secondary stock
0% LVR gives flexibility to fund leasing incentives from cash without refinancing risk, and removes forced-seller risk pending the eventual sale

Centuria NZ manages roughly 80 properties and NZ$2.4bn AUM (parent Centuria Capital ~AU$21.8bn), giving market insight and leasing relationships, but this benefit accrues largely to the manager rather than translating into a durable advantage for a single-building shareholder vehicle that is about to be wound up
As a Portfolio Investment Entity, distributions can be treated as excluded income for NZ tax purposes, a modest structural benefit for domestic retail holders but not a competitive or economic moat

weaknesses: Single asset, single sub-market (North Shore Auckland office) concentration risk with no diversification
Sub-scale for a listed vehicle - fixed corporate costs (directors, audit, listing/registry fees, insurance) are large relative to a $105.5m asset base and shrinking equity

External management by Centuria (a 19.99% shareholder via Centuria Capital (NZ) No.1 Ltd, held just below the 20% takeover-code threshold) creates a related-party/conflict-of-interest dynamic on fees, leasing decisions and eventual sale/wind-up timing; a Centuria-linked director is no longer classified as independent (from Oct-2025)

High vacancy (75.6% occupied at Mar-2026, up from 65.0%, but still ~3,552m2 vacant) leaves earnings and valuation exposed to a soft Albany office leasing market (vacancy rose from 9.5% to 11.7% in the wider market over H2 2025)
No pipeline for growth - company is explicitly not seeking new acquisitions or development opportunities; every dollar of leasing capex is spent solely to prepare the single asset for sale

growth_drivers: NOT a growth story: Asset Plus is on an explicit lease-up, sell, and wind-up trajectory - there is no acquisition or expansion strategy, and none should be expected. 'Growth drivers' below refer only to value-realization steps within the wind-down, not to a compounding business

Near-term focus is completing lease-up of Munroe Lane's remaining vacant space (Levels 1, 2 and part of 6), which would lift occupancy from 75.6% toward full occupancy and support a stronger eventual sale valuation
MILK Orthodontics lease (12-year term, ground floor) expected to commence 'in the coming months' per the FY2026 Chairman's letter, sustaining occupancy at 75.6% once operational
Fully-leased passing net rent potential of $7.1-7.2m versus current passing net rent of ~$5.2m implies meaningful upside to income and valuation if remaining vacancy is resolved

Eventual catalyst is sale of Munroe Lane followed by capital return/wind-up, which the Board has repeatedly reaffirmed (including at the 6-Aug-2026 AGM) will require a shareholder vote once leasing is sufficiently advanced - this remains the key value-realization event rather than organic growth

The FY2027 quarterly dividend increase to 0.25 cps (from 0.20 cps), announced in August 2026, signals management's view that underlying FFO has stepped up following the Aderant lease commencement, but this is a cash-return decision, not a growth signal

business.description: 100% of the portfolio is one Auckland office building; any tenant default, structural issue, or local market deterioration disproportionately impacts the whole company

Occupancy only 75.6% at Mar-2026 (and that figure includes an unconditional-but-not-yet-commenced MILK Orthodontics lease); Albany/North Shore office vacancy rose from 9.5% to 11.7% (Jun-Dec 2025) per CBRE, with limited large-scale tenant demand and competing sublease space undermining lease-up

Centuria (through its NZ manager and as a 19.99% shareholder, held just under the 20% takeover threshold) earns management fees ($0.54m in FY26) irrespective of shareholder outcomes, and has board representation that is no longer deemed independent (from Oct-2025), creating potential misalignment on fee levels, leasing capex decisions and the timing of a sale/wind-up

Directors' fees, audit fees, listing/registry fees and insurance (~$1.39m total FY26 admin costs) are a high fixed drag on a single, shrinking asset base, eroding NTA over time even before revaluation losses

financial.description: NTA has declined from 38.9 cps (Mar-2024) to 32.4 cps (Mar-2025) to 30.7 cps (Mar-2026), driven by capitalisation-rate softening and capex/leasing incentives capitalised into the valuation base that are not fully recovered in rent

$3.01m of leasing incentives/costs were incurred in FY26 alone, funded from the $6.93m cash balance; further incentives will be needed to lease remaining vacant space, directly reducing the cash available for eventual distribution

Dividends are explicitly 'subject to quarterly review'; while the rate was just raised to 0.25 cps for FY2027 (Aug-2026, from 0.20 cps) on stronger FFO, it is not a guaranteed or contractual payout and could still be cut if further leasing incentives consume cash faster than expected

regulatory.description: Any sale of Munroe Lane or subsequent wind-up requires a shareholder vote, which introduces process risk, timing uncertainty, and the possibility that a transaction is delayed or rejected

~$13.1m of gross tax losses exist, of which $10.59m remain unrecognised as a deferred tax asset; their eventual utilisation (or forfeiture on wind-up/ownership change) affects realisable shareholder value

The company's Portfolio Investment Entity tax status underpins its tax-efficient distribution profile; a sale/wind-up process or ownership changes (e.g., Centuria crossing the 20% takeover threshold) could have PIE eligibility or Takeovers Code implications

macro.description: Elevated capitalisation/discount rates and soft office demand have driven three consecutive years of unrealised valuation losses ($7.43m FY26, $7.16m FY25, $4.90m FY24); a prolonged high-rate, weak-demand environment continues to pressure both income and asset value

Property valuations are directly sensitive to capitalisation and discount rate assumptions used by independent valuers (Bayleys); further softening would flow through to further NTA erosion, though the company itself is currently debt-free

Hybrid/remote work trends and oversupply of secondary office and sublease space in the North Shore market continue to constrain rental growth and lengthen lease-up periods; the Chairman's FY2026 letter also cited Middle East-driven macro/energy uncertainty as a further drag on tenant confidence during the year

macro_factors.industry_outlook: NZ commercial (office) property remains in a cyclical downturn with elevated vacancy, soft rental growth, and valuers applying softer capitalisation/discount rates; a broader NZ rate-cutting cycle has provided some relief but office sector recovery has lagged industrial/retail, and the North Shore/Albany submarket specifically saw vacancy rise from 9.5% to 11.7% over H2 2025
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - direct exposure to a single office asset in a market experiencing above-average vacancy and negative valuation momentum for three consecutive years
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High indirect sensitivity via property capitalisation/discount rates used in valuations, despite the company itself carrying zero debt (0% LVR) and no direct interest rate/refinancing risk
key_input_costs: Leasing incentives and tenant fit-out capex
Property operating expenses/outgoings on vacant space

recent_developments.event: Settled sale of 35 Graham Street; used proceeds to repay all bank debt, reducing LVR to 0%
Paid a special dividend of 5.0 cents per share following the Graham Street sale
A Centuria board nominee ceased to be classified as an independent director, reflecting Centuria's dual role as manager and 19.99% shareholder
New Aderant lease commenced across half of Level 6 (10-year term), lifting occupancy to ~74.3%

FY2026 annual results: FFO improved to $3.18m (from $0.53m), but AFFO fell to just $0.17m after $3.01m of leasing incentives/costs; total comprehensive loss narrowed to $3.16m (from $5.70m); NTA declined to 30.7 cps (from 32.4 cps) on a $7.43m unrealised revaluation loss; WALE 9.4 years

Munroe Lane independently revalued at $105.5m (from $107.0m), reflecting softer capitalisation/discount rates plus capitalised leasing capex; MILK Orthodontics secured for a 12-year ground-floor lease (not yet commenced), lifting prospective occupancy to 75.6%
Quarterly dividend of 0.20 cents per share paid for the March 2026 quarter
Director nominations closed ahead of the 2026 Annual Meeting

2026 Annual Meeting of Shareholders held at Munroe Lane, Albany, Auckland (in person and virtual); routine business including re-election of director Carol Campbell and auditor fee approval; Bruce Cotterill remains Chairman; Board reiterated the lease-up-then-sell-then-wind-up strategy; no sale, wind-up resolution, takeover approach or scheme of arrangement has been announced as of this writing

Board lifted the quarterly dividend to 0.25 cents per share for the FY2027 March quarter (up from 0.20 cps), citing higher FFO following the Aderant lease commencement; the increase applies from the first FY2027 quarterly payment and dividends remain subject to quarterly review with no imputation credits attached

Board continues to state that once Munroe Lane is sufficiently leased it will look to sell the property, with any sale or subsequent wind-up requiring a shareholder vote - both decisions likely to be put to shareholders together; no fixed timetable has been disclosed

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Results (22-May-2026) and August 2026 dividend announcement / AGM

items.target: Complete lease-up of Munroe Lane, then sell the property and put a wind-up of the Company to shareholders
items.period: No fixed date - contingent on leasing progress and market conditions
items.notes: Reaffirmed at the 6-Aug-2026 AGM. This is the single most important guidance item for valuation purposes - the company should be assessed as an NTA/liquidation-value story, not a perpetual going-concern DCF.

items.target: 0.25 cents per share (first FY2027 quarter; ex-div 14-Aug-2026, paid 26-Aug-2026)
items.notes: Up from 0.20 cps paid for the March 2026 quarter. Board cited higher FFO following the Aderant lease commencement. Still explicitly 'subject to quarterly review' - no fixed forward payout policy; no imputation credits attached, though distributions benefit from the Company's PIE tax status.

items.target: Future leasing costs and incentives to be funded entirely from existing cash reserves ($6.93m at Mar-2026), without drawing debt
items.notes: No new debt facility contemplated; company intends to remain unleveraged through to sale

items.target: Full occupancy of Munroe Lane (currently 75.6%, ~3,552m2 vacant across Levels 1, 2 and 6)
items.period: No fixed date - MILK Orthodontics lease expected 'in the coming months' as of the May-2026 annual report; no update on commencement as of Aug-2026
items.notes: Fully-leased net rent potential estimated at $7.1-7.2m vs current passing net rent of ~$5.2m

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Bruce Cotterill (FY2026 annual report, reaffirmed at the Aug-2026 AGM): leasing the balance of Munroe Lane remains the primary focus; market conditions remain challenging with limited large-occupier demand and elevated Albany office vacancy (11.7% as at Dec-2025, up from 9.5% in Jun-2025), compounded by broader macro uncertainty (cited Middle East-related energy/supply-chain impacts on business confidence); the Board remains confident management is delivering the best possible outcome for shareholders and reiterates that any sale of Munroe Lane or subsequent wind-up of the Company will require shareholder approval, likely voted on together. The subsequent decision to lift the quarterly dividend to 0.25 cps in August 2026 signals incremental confidence in the improved FFO run-rate post-Aderant, without altering the underlying wind-down endgame.

bull_case: Trades at a very large discount to net tangible assets (share price ~NZ$0.17-0.175 vs NTA of $0.307 per share as of Mar-2026, i.e. roughly 43-45% below stated book value), offering potential value realization if the eventual sale price is close to book
Debt-free balance sheet (0% LVR) with ~$6.9m of cash provides a funded runway to complete lease-up without dilutive refinancing or forced asset sales

Clear, management-articulated endgame (lease-up, sell, wind up, return capital), reaffirmed at the Aug-2026 AGM, gives a defined catalyst path rather than open-ended going-concern uncertainty, appealing to value/special-situations investors

Recent leasing momentum (Aderant 10-year lease from Feb-2026, MILK Orthodontics 12-year lease pending) is narrowing the vacancy gap, lengthened WALE to 9.4 years, and supported an August-2026 dividend increase to 0.25 cps - tangible evidence the cash-flow story is improving even as book value has not yet stabilised

5 Star Green Star building targeting a 5-star NABERSNZ rating is well-positioned versus older, less sustainable competing office stock for the tenants that remain in the market, which should support a comparatively better exit valuation
PIE tax structure means distributions can be treated as excluded income for NZ shareholders, a modest but real after-tax yield enhancement versus a company-taxed dividend
bear_case: This is a wind-down vehicle, not a growth or income compounder - shareholders are essentially waiting on an asset sale and liquidation at an uncertain future date, with no organic growth in earnings power and no acquisition strategy

AFFO (true cash profit after leasing costs) was only $0.17m in FY26 - the improved FFO headline masks the fact that leasing incentives continue to consume nearly all operating cash flow, and further incentives will likely be needed to complete lease-up of the remaining ~3,552m2

NTA has fallen for three consecutive years (38.9 cps to 32.4 cps to 30.7 cps) on capitalisation-rate softening and capitalised leasing costs; there is no guarantee the eventual sale price will match, let alone exceed, the current independent valuation, and the market's 43-45% discount to NTA suggests investors already doubt it will

External management by Centuria (a 19.99% shareholder, positioned just under the 20% Takeovers Code threshold) creates conflict-of-interest risk around fee levels, capex decisions and the pace/timing of the wind-up, and Centuria's board nominee is no longer classified as independent (from Oct-2025)
Sub-scale corporate overhead (directors, audit, listing/insurance costs of ~$1.39m/yr) is a persistent drag on a single, currently ~$105.5m shrinking asset base

Continued high vacancy (75.6%, and that figure relies on a not-yet-commenced MILK Orthodontics lease) in a soft North Shore Auckland office market (vacancy rising to 11.7%) creates real risk that lease-up stalls, further eroding both income and the eventual realisable sale value; no sale, wind-up timetable, or takeover approach has yet been announced, so the value-realization catalyst remains open-ended
